checks.s: The memo is addressed to Marcus Yardley.
The memo is addressed to Diane Suh.
The memo is addressed to Anton Prewitt.
The memo is addressed to Rachel Guzmán.
The memo is addressed to General Counsel Theodore 'Ted' Calloway or Ted Calloway.
The memo identifies Priya Nandakumar as its author or preparer and gives her title as Vice President & Associate General Counsel or substantively equivalent wording.
The memo refers to the separately managed account as SMA-VII.
The memo identifies Thalweg Public Employees' Retirement System or Thalweg PERS as the institutional limited partner or counterparty.
The memo identifies management fee as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo identifies investment period termination as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo identifies GP removal as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo identifies key person as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo identifies indemnification as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo identifies co-investment/MFN as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo identifies carried interest as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo identifies portfolio transparency/reporting as an out-of-policy IMA term category.
The memo states that the LP proposes a 1.00% management fee on committed capital during the investment period.
The memo states that the LP proposes a 0.65% post-investment-period management fee on net invested cost.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix investment-period management fee floor is 1.25% on committed capital.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix post-investment-period management fee floor is 1.00% on invested capital.
The memo explicitly notes that the LP's markup changes the post-investment-period fee basis from 'invested capital' to 'net invested cost'.
The memo identifies the LP's proposed investment-period termination right as unilateral and LP-initiated.
The memo states that the LP's proposed no-cause investment-period termination right may be exercised after 3 years.
The memo states that the LP's proposed right requires 90 days' written notice.
The memo states that the LP may exercise the proposed right without cause.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix permits no-cause termination no earlier than the 4th anniversary of the investment period.
The memo identifies the proposed GP removal right as unilateral and exercisable by a single LP.
The memo identifies the proposed GP removal right as no-fault, or not for cause.
The memo states that the proposed GP removal right requires 180 days' notice.
The memo states that the proposed GP removal right is exercisable after year 3.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix permits GP removal only for cause and requires a minimum voting threshold of 66.67% in interest.
The memo discusses a qualitative risk of granting a single investor no-fault GP removal authority, such as precedent risk, leverage asymmetry, governance implications, or impact on fund stability.
The memo states that the LP's key person clause automatically suspends upon the departure of any 1 of 4 named key persons.
The memo lists Marcus Yardley as a key person in the LP markup.
The memo lists Diane Suh as a key person in the LP markup.
The memo lists Anton Prewitt as a key person in the LP markup.
The memo lists Lena Kovaçi as a key person in the LP markup.
The memo states that the LP's key person provision includes a 90-day cure period.
The memo states that the LP's key person provision allows full termination if the event is not cured within that period.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix permits a key person trigger upon the departure of any 2 of 3 named key persons.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix requires a key person cure period of not less than 120 days.
The memo separately identifies the expansion of the named key person list beyond the standard three to include a fourth person, Lena Kovaçi, as a concern or deviation.
The memo identifies that the LP's markup adds simple negligence, distinct from gross negligence, to the carve-outs from GP indemnification.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix does not permit indemnification carve-outs beyond the standard carve-outs of fraud, gross negligence, and willful misconduct.
The memo identifies that the LP's markup caps the LP's indemnification obligations at the LP's unfunded commitment.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix requires LP indemnification obligations to remain uncapped.
The memo identifies that the LP demands a contractual right to co-invest up to 100% of any single deal.
The memo identifies that the LP's proposed co-investment has zero management fee and zero carried interest.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix limits co-investment to 50% of deal equity at a reduced management fee of 0.50%.
The memo identifies that the LP's MFN clause extends across all Crestfall-managed vehicles, not only the SMA-VII vehicle.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix restricts MFN rights to the SMA-VII vehicle only.

The memo discusses the systemic risk that a cross-vehicle MFN clause poses to Crestfall's other fund vehicles, such as cascading concessions, effects on existing LP economics, or constraints on future fund terms.
The memo identifies that the LP proposes 15% carried interest, below the Fallback Authority Matrix minimum of 17.5%.
The memo identifies that the LP proposes a 9% preferred return, above the Fallback Authority Matrix maximum of 8.5%.
The memo identifies that the LP's markup eliminates the GP catch-up entirely, contrary to the Fallback Authority Matrix requirement of a 100% GP catch-up.
The memo identifies that the LP proposes a clawback escrow of 100% of all carried interest distributions, exceeding the Fallback Authority Matrix maximum of 50% of net carried interest distributions.
The memo identifies that the LP's proposed 10-business-day portfolio reporting delivery window is more aggressive than the Fallback Authority Matrix's permitted 30-calendar-day delivery window.
The memo identifies that the requirement to deliver underlying portfolio company financial statements to a single LP is not authorized by the Fallback Authority Matrix.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the management fee terms.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the investment period termination terms.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the GP removal terms.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the key person terms.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the indemnification terms.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the co-investment/MFN terms.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the carried interest terms.
The memo gives an explicit recommendation to accept, counter-propose, or reject the portfolio transparency/reporting terms.
For each out-of-policy term for which the memo recommends a counter-proposal, the counter-proposal includes specific parameters, such as rates, thresholds, time periods, or structural terms.
The memo references the next Investment Committee meeting scheduled for June 18, 2025.
The memo references Thalweg PERS's hard deadline of June 30, 2025, for IMA execution.
The memo connects the June 18, 2025 Investment Committee meeting and the June 30, 2025 hard deadline to explain the urgency of obtaining approval.
The memo identifies the Thalweg PERS commitment amount for SMA-VII as $175,000,000 or $175 million.
The memo notes that SMA-VII would represent Crestfall's largest single separately managed account.
The memo states that Crestfall's current total AUM across all vehicles is approximately $2.4 billion.
The memo expressly identifies Fallback Authority Matrix v.4.2 as the governing policy against which deviations are measured.
The memo states that the Fallback Authority Matrix v.4.2 was approved by the Investment Committee on March 14, 2024.
The memo identifies IMA Draft 3, or Draft 3 of the Investment Management Agreement, as the marked-up document under review.
The memo identifies Bridlewood Haines LLP as the outside counsel that prepared and submitted the IMA markup.
The memo states that the IMA Draft 3 markup was received or delivered on June 4, 2025.
